newsitem.title: USA: NYC comptroller sees stronger economy in jobs data.
newsitem.headline: NYC comptroller sees stronger economy in jobs data.

text.p: The New York City Comptroller on Thursday said that although the unemployment rate in February stayed high at 9.4 percent, enough new jobs were being added to keep the economic recovery going.

New York City added 4,100 new jobs in February, with the private sector accounting for most of the growth--3,400 positions--as public services only gained 700, a study by Comptroller Alan Hevesi found.
And one sector, retailing, accounted for the vast majority of hiring, adding 3,100 jobs, the highest gain in two years.
"This is continuing evidence that New York City's economy continues to show signs of recovery, though there's much work to be done to create more job opportunities," said Hevesi, in prepared remarks.
Hevesi noted that New York City's unemployment rate has not been this high since March 1994, and for the past 12 months, has stayed above 8.5 percent.
